.claude-plugin/commands/docs-fleet.md, .cursor-plugin/commands/docs-fleet.md, .gemini-extension/commands/docs-fleet.toml, .antigravity-extension/commands/docs-fleet.toml (regenerated slash commands, all platforms via generate:plugin:all)

adr.rationale: docs-fleet introduces no new family-level decision; it references the existing family ADRs (0087 fan-out, 0088 front-load/park, 0105 claim-lease). Like the other quality-queue members (cleanup-fleet, test-fleet, craft-fleet) it ships as a member with a proposal + plan and adds no ADR. The one genuine decision — standalone vs fold — is member-scoped and resolved in proposal.md, not a family ADR.

parkedForks.fork: Fold-vs-standalone (roadmap shard #1230 deferred blocker): fold doc-drift into cleanup-fleet and doc-quality into craft-fleet, vs ship docs-fleet as a standalone member.
parkedForks.resolution: Resolved to STANDALONE per the parent roadmap-fleet directive and argued in proposal.md (disjoint queues; floor-vs-ceiling is the family's own line; conveyor symmetry). Recorded here rather than parked because the directive settled the default; the SKILL.md Boundary section + scope-creep Rationalization enforce the non-overlap in practice.

assumptions: The parent roadmap-fleet lane directive resolves the roadmap shard's deferred fold-vs-standalone blocker in favour of a standalone member; proposal.md argues why standalone (not fold) is correct.

docs-fleet is a quality-queue member (off the core spine) modeled on cleanup-fleet — a single-pipeline convergence-remediation fan-out — so item-type routing (ADR 0103) is N/A: there is exactly one per-area pipeline (harness-docs-pipeline --fix), not a bug/spec-ready/feature router.

A doc area carries no GitHub-native id at SELECT, so docs-fleet uses only the claim-lease's open-PR-cross-check degradation (spine § Cross-run claim lease), not the full label+comment lease reserved for the ID-based members.

Platform mirrors are symlinks to the canonical claude-code skill dir; editing SKILL.md/skill.yaml updates all four, and the gemini/antigravity .toml + per-platform slash commands regenerate via the generators/pre-commit — mirrors are never hand-forked.

No @harness-engineering/<pkg>/src or package.json is touched (pure skill + generated-docs change), so an empty changeset is the correct honest no-release acknowledgement per scripts/check-changesets.mjs; it does not bump or release any package.

The deliverable is authored markdown/yaml (skill contract), not executable orchestrator code — consistent with every existing -fleet member; the spine's Workflow primitive is the named future deterministic upgrade, out of scope for this slice.
